the sarcolemma of cow myometrium contains a system of antiport which is capable of Ca2+ uptake against the concentration gradient and is not sensitive to the membrane potential sign and to temperature changes.
the myometrial tissue contains a system which possesses a low-affinity for Ca2+ ions and protects myocytes from the damaging action of Ca2+.

the myometrial sarcolemma possesses a system of non-eletrogenic Ca(2+)-Na(+) antiport, which is not potential-dependent and is not involved in the regulation of the transmembrane transport processes of Ca(2+).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the role of the electric field in the regulation of intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis.
the mechanism of Ca2+ transport into the sarcolemma fraction of cow uterus smooth muscle.
the properties of Ca2+ transport systems of the sarcolemma of cow myometrium cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sarcolemma of myometrium tissue has a Ca2+-antiport system with the potential-independent transport of Ca2+.
the sarcolemma of cow myometrium cells contains a system of Ca2+ antiport which is independent on the membrane potential and which possesses a low Ca2+ affinity.
the sarcolemmal Na+-Ca2+ antiporter of the smooth muscle is a potential-independent, non-electrogenic transport system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Na+/Ca2+ antiport in the myometrium sarcomere is not a potential-dependent system and that the Na+-stimulation of Ca2+ efflux from the sarcolemmal fraction does not occur at the expense of the electric field energy.
the sarcolemma possesses a Ca2+/Na+ antiporter, which is not dependent on the membrane potential and does not utilize the energy of transmembrane potential.

Na+-stimulated Ca2+ transport in polarized sarcolemmal membranes of smooth muscle is independent of the membrane potential and is not accompanied by the transmembrane transport and accumulation of Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sarcolemma of myometrium tissue is characterized by the presence of a Ca2+ transport system which is independent of membrane potential, i.e., a non-electrogenic antiport.
a non-electrogenic Ca2+-Na+ antiport exists in the smooth muscle cell membrane.
the Na+-stimulation of Ca2+ transport is potential-independent and does not obey the simple diffusion kinetics.
